course_title: Impact Academy 3: Delivering and Capturing New Values
course_description: In this applied course, students will learn how to deploy and capture value from a new idea, product, service or business model that solves an unresolved problem or exploits an unrealised opportunity. Students will be mentored as they seek to systematically implement, iterate and validate their strategy/business model, and endeavour to achieve external validation through external customer, investor or stakeholder engagement and commitment.

This course is being delivered as a combination of in class seminars, mentoring and participation in the Empower program run by UQ Ventures. Students are expected to actively participate across each of these learning opportunities.
course_aims: This course provides students who have discovered and designed a desirable, feasible and viable intervention in MGTS7821 Impact Academy 2, the opportunity to develop and deploy an innovative solution into the marketplace. Students will learn to navigate and mitigate the risks and complexities of validating and implementing new value creation strategies with a sustainable impact in an ethical and socially responsible manner.

learning_outcomes.description: Develop and implement a cogent and competitive strategy to exploit an identified opportunity.
Working individually or in teams, engage, influence and secure support from a network of stakeholders to enable execution of the value creation strategy.

Build a coalition which is committed to delivering new value to multiple stakeholders with ethical and socially responsible leadership demonstrated through humility, empathy, authenticity, and agility.

assessment_details.submission_guidelines:
Students are to submit their presentation via Blackboard prior to presenting
Deferral or extension
You may be able to apply for an extension .
The maximum extension allowed is 14 days. Extensions are given in multiples of 24 hours.
This assessment presents the state of evidence behind your business model at week 5: the assumptions you have already tested, and the test program you now have in place for the remainder of the semester.
The presentation has two parts. Results to date covers the business model assumptions you have already put in front of reality — through customer conversations, outreach, sales attempts, product experiments and early usage, whether before the course or during it. For each, you present the evidence you gathered, what it did and did not support, and what you changed or deliberately retained in your business model as a result. Tests planned covers the riskiest assumptions still standing and the experiments you have designed to test them: what each test involves, the metric and threshold that will count as a meaningful result, when it will run, and what each outcome would mean for the venture.
If you are unable to attend your presentation, please advise your Course Coordinator on or before the due date.

assessment_details.title: Venture Build Workbook
assessment_details.other_conditions: Longitudinal, Secure. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: The Venture Build Workbook is the major assessment item for this course. It is the structured, cumulative record you maintain across the semester while developing your own venture: the experiments you run, the evidence you gather, the decisions you make, and your reflection on what the evidence tells you. You submit the completed workbook at the end of the course, and it is assessed as a whole. This is a practice-based, evidence-led assessment. You are a practising founder working on a real venture; the workbook captures your applied work as you progress through a structured program. Read full task description Hide full task description
